headline: Fed's Williams Sees No Need for Dramatic Interest Rate Increase
summary: New York Fed President John Williams stated that while the U.S. central bank still has work to do to return inflation to its 2% target, the current economic situation does not require a sharp interest rate hike.
why: Federal Reserve officials' commentary on monetary policy direction guides market expectations for benchmark interest rates and borrowing costs.

impacts.name: US Federal Funds Rate
impacts.why: Central bank commentary signals that aggressive monetary tightening is not currently warranted.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Remarks from Federal Reserve officials indicating that inflation control does not require dramatic rate hikes help stabilize rate expectations across debt markets.
